paper.authors_full: Harsh Kumar, Jonathan Vincentius, Ewan Jordan, Ashton Anderson
paper.title: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25), Yokohama, Japan
paper.pdf_filename: Kumar Vincentius Jordan Anderson (2025) - Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs.pdf
paper.version_read: arXiv:2410.03703v2 [cs.HC], 15 Feb 2025 (PDF p. 1 side stamp); CHI '25 formatted paper, DOI 10.1145/3706598.3714198. The ACM version of record was not separately compared.
paper.one_line_finding: After AI was removed, AUT originality was lower with prior GPT-4o strategies than with no AI (Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 9.14, p = 0.010; Dunn p = 0.009) and did not differ with prior GPT-4o idea lists (p = 1.000) (p. 7), and RAT accuracy was lower with prior GPT-4o guidance than with no AI (Tukey p = 0.005; mean difference -10.6, 95% CI [-18.6, -2.7]) and did not differ with prior GPT-4o answers (p = 0.682) (p. 11).

studies.label: Experiment 1 (divergent thinking, Alternate Uses Test)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.5; PDF p. 4, Figure 2 and Section 3.1.1 (random assignment of the recruited cohort)

arms.name: None
arms.description: No LLM support during exposure or test; also labeled No LLM Response in the paper.

arms.name: List of Ideas
arms.description: Seven randomly sampled GPT-4o alternate uses shown per exposure object; participants could use them in their responses. Static content supplied by the study, not open chat (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1.1).

arms.name: List of Strategies
arms.description: Seven GPT-4o SCAMPER strategies per exposure object; prompts and questions without example answers. This arm is a coach under the codebook (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1.1; PDF p. 16, Figure 11).

studies.task: Generate creative alternate uses for everyday objects in three exposure rounds under the assigned assistance, followed by a one-minute Snake distractor and one unassisted test round with a new object.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (gpt-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 16, Appendix A.1.1 (model version and date of use; release year not printed)

preregistration.where: https://aspredicted.org/dkvp-n785.pdf; PDF p. 4, footnote 1; PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.4. The linked PDF could not be retrieved during reconciliation (socket access blocked).
preregistration.primary_outcome: Originality of ideas in the unassisted AUT test round, identified from the primary unassisted phase in Figure 1 (PDF p. 1) and the preregistered originality analysis in Section 3.1.4 (PDF p. 6); the external registration was not independently inspected.

studies.label: Experiment 2 (convergent thinking, Remote Associates Test)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 4.1.5; PDF p. 9, Figure 7 and Section 4.1.1 (random assignment of the recruited cohort)
counts_source.quote: We recruited 640 participants from Prolific (of whom 99% passed the attention check).

arms.name: None
arms.description: No LLM support during exposure or test; also labeled No LLM Response in the paper.

arms.name: LLM Answer
arms.description: GPT-4o answer to each exposure RAT problem, supplied in a fixed response panel and available for participants to use (PDF p. 9, Section 4.1.1).

arms.name: LLM Guidance
arms.description: GPT-4o lists five associated words per cue word and encourages finding a connection. The prompt asks it not to give the solution directly, but Table 2 includes the solution snow among the guidance words. It supplies candidate words and is not content-free coaching (PDF p. 9, Section 4.1.1; PDF p. 16, Figure 12; PDF p. 18, Table 2).

studies.task: Solve three Remote Associates Test word-association problems under the assigned assistance, followed by a one-minute Snake distractor and two unassisted test problems.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (gpt-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 16, Appendix B.1.1 (model version and date of use; release year not printed)

preregistration.where: https://aspredicted.org/4q75-bskd.pdf; PDF p. 9, footnote 2; PDF p. 11, Sections 4.1.4-4.1.5. The linked PDF could not be retrieved during reconciliation (socket access blocked).
preregistration.primary_outcome: Accuracy on the unassisted RAT test problems, identified from the primary unassisted phase in Figure 1 (PDF p. 1) and the preregistered accuracy analysis in Sections 4.1.4-4.1.5 (PDF p. 11); the external registration was not independently inspected.

estimates.measure_detail: Originality of each participant-submitted AUT idea, scored by the existing fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier trained on human originality judgments on a scale of 1 to 5 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3). estimates.notes: Bonferroni-adjusted Dunn pairwise p-value. The originality score is defined per idea, but the observation used by the test and any participant averaging are unspecified; unit is null. se_basis is not_reported because the basis of the reported p-value is unidentified. estimates.measure_detail: Median pairwise cosine distance between SBERT embeddings of the ideas in one participant's idea set for the test object (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3). estimates.notes: Bonferroni-adjusted Dunn pairwise p-value. This is variety within one person's ideas, coded flexibility, with one test-round idea set per participant. The observation and uncertainty basis are participant. The higher_is code more_creative denotes greater within-person flexibility. Its preregistered-primary status could not be confirmed from the paper; the linked preregistration was inaccessible, so not_stated is used. open_items: Neither experiment prints analyzed participant counts or arm-specific randomized/analyzed counts. The study n_randomized values are the recruited cohorts shown in the randomization flow, not counts for a particular pairwise analysis. Attention-check percentages and degrees of freedom are not converted to counts (PDF pp. 4, 6, 9 and 11).

No eligible outcome has numerically printed arm means, SDs or SEs. Figures 4, 5 and 9 have no numeric point labels. Figure 5 defines one-SE bars; Figures 4 and 9 do not define their bars. No figure values were digitized.

The analysis units for S1 originality, S1 creative flexibility and S2 RAT accuracy are not explicitly stated; unit is null. Per-idea scoring and repeated-answer degrees of freedom are not treated as confirmation of the statistical observation. The uncertainty basis is not_reported when it cannot be identified, including records retaining printed p-values or a confidence interval.

Exposure fluency and individual-level diversity are defined per participant-round, but the paper does not specify averaging within people or treatment of repeated rounds. The participant unit category is retained; participant-level uncertainty is not asserted.

Group-level diversity uses Monte Carlo idea subsets. The exact number of set scores per arm, item and phase and dependence across resamples are not reported. Set is the nearest unit code, and these results do not establish participant-level uncertainty (PDF pp. 6-8).

Creative flexibility is defined using maximum cosine similarity but described in the results as dissimilarity. The transformation and whose exposure ideas enter the reference set are not specified. Direction follows the explicit results statement; construct flexibility follows the participant-oriented interpretation (PDF pp. 6-8).

The RAT Guidance-versus-None mean difference is not explicitly labeled with a unit in the result sentence. Its covariate adjustment and whether the confidence interval is simultaneous Tukey coverage are unspecified. No rescaling, SE or standardized effect is calculated (PDF p. 11).

The codebook has no dedicated measure code for answer-key accuracy. automated_score is retained as the screening form convention for RAT accuracy without asserting use of an LLM or another scoring model (PDF p. 9, Section 4.1).

The linked preregistration PDFs were each attempted with urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 during reconciliation; both were blocked by socket permissions (WinError 10013). The paper supports the main unassisted originality and accuracy outcomes; other unassisted outcomes have preregistered_primary not_stated because their status could not be independently confirmed.
The paper gives GPT-4o's date of use, but not its release year; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 16, Appendices A.1.1 and B.1.1).
The frequency with which LLM Guidance contained the correct RAT answer is unreported. Table 2 includes the solution among the candidate words for one example (PDF p. 18).
The saved arXiv v2 PDF was checked; the ACM version of record was not separately compared.
